newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian metalworkers seen poised for second strike.
newsitem.headline: Italian metalworkers seen poised for second strike.

text.p: Italian metalworker unions are poised to call a second strike over their pay dispute with management, industrial sources said on Tuesday.

Leaders from the three main metal unions, which represent workers from most major Italian industrial concerns, are due to meet on Thursday and are set to call an eight hour stoppage for November 15, sources said.

Negotiations between trade unions and employers over the renewal of contracts for some 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers broke down last month and unions staged an initial eight hour strike on September 27.
Union sources said they saw no prospects for a fresh round of wage negotiations with employers before Thursday and added that neither side had formally requested talks.
"Both sides talk of a generic willingness to pick-up the negotiations, but there is stalemate," a union source said.
Unions have asked for a 262,000 lire pay increase to cover the 1997-98 period, of which 97,000 lire would cover higher-than-expected inflation in the 1995-96 period.

The Italian metal industry employers' association, Federmeccanica, has rejected this demand, saying it would effectively increase the cost of labour by an average 20 percent for the three year period 1996-98.
Target inflation for the same three year period is just 8.4 percent. Employers have offered workers 180,000 lire.
The dispute has turned into a battle of wills to see which definition of a 1993 wage accord between government, unions and employers should be honoured.
Unions say the accord stipulates that any shortfall between real and government-targeted inflation in the preceding contract period should be recouped in successive pay deals. Employers dispute this.
A number of other sectors are awaiting the outcome of the metal workers dispute before completing their own round of pay negotiations. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
